guideTitle: Best Portable Jobsite Table Saws Under $600 (2026)
metaDescription: Five portable jobsite table saws at or under $600 from Bosch, DEWALT, SKIL, Evolution and MarvTool, compared on rip capacity, fence quality and stand design.
expertTake: The Bosch GTS15-10 is the pick for most buyers because a 32-1/8 inch rip capacity, a rack and pinion fence and a blade brake that stops the blade in about three seconds add up to a saw that is both capable and calm. The Evolution R10TBLX is the value pick if you want a wheeled stand, dado plate and crosscut sled included. Skip a jobsite saw altogether if you rip full sheets of hardwood plywood daily, because a contractor or cabinet saw with a larger table and a heavier fence holds a straight line far better.
introParagraphs: A jobsite table saw trades table size and weight for portability, so the blade spins in a compact body that fits in a truck and sets up on a folding stand. The practical differences between models are not motor size but fence quality, rip capacity and how stable the saw feels when a sheet of plywood is pushed through it.

This guide explains what the upper end of a larger budget buys in a jobsite saw, why fence design and guarding matter more than amps, and where lighter portable designs give up accuracy. The picks are listed above, with the reviews below. Listing prices move, and the cap reflects prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: BOSCH GTS15-10 10 Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Wheeled Stand, 32-1/8 Inch Rip

specList.label: Fence
specList.value: Rack and pinion with color-coded index pins

products.description:
A rack and pinion fence moves with a gear, so both ends of the fence travel together and stay parallel to the blade, and color-coded index pins mark common widths so you can set a rip quickly. The 32-1/8 inch rip capacity is the widest in this roundup, enough to rip a half sheet of plywood without a track. A brake stops the 3,800 RPM blade in about three seconds after you release the switch, which cuts the time the blade is a hazard.

Compared with the DEWALT DWE7485, which rips 24.5 inches, the Bosch handles wider stock. Against the Evolution R10TBLX, it offers a more refined fence and brake but no dado plate or sled in the listing. The listing's horsepower figure is a peak claim, so judge the saw by its 15 amp rating instead. For a remodeler who rips plywood and lumber on site, it is the most capable choice.

Ownership: align the blade to the miter slot when the saw arrives, and check the fence for parallel at several widths. Keep the rack and pinion clean of dust, and wax the table. Replace the stock blade with a quality 40 to 50 tooth blade for smoother rips, and always use the riving knife and guard, since a table saw that kicks back does so in a split second.
products.bestFor: Remodelers and serious DIYers who rip plywood and lumber on site and want a refined fence.
pros: 32-1/8 inch rip capacity handles half sheets of plywood
Rack and pinion fence stays parallel with index pins
Brake stops the blade in about three seconds
Wheeled stand makes the saw easy to move
cons: Heavier than the compact DEWALT and MarvTool saws
No dado plate or sled in the listing
Horsepower claim is a peak figure, not a continuous one

products.name: Evolution R10TBLX 10 Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Wheeled Stand and Dado Plate

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Zero-clearance plate, dado plate, crosscut sled

products.description:
Soft start ramps the motor up slowly instead of slamming to full speed, which reduces the jolt of a 15 amp motor on a shared circuit and also lowers the torque kick when the switch is flipped. The package includes a zero-clearance throat plate, a rack and pinion fence, a crosscut sled and a dado plate, which together make it a more complete woodworking saw than most jobsite models. A multi-material blade lets the saw cut wood, plastic and some metals.

The tradeoff is brand support and refinement. The Evolution lacks the proven fence feel of the Bosch GTS15-10 and the brake. Compared with the Evolution R10TS, the R10TBLX adds the wheeled stand. Compared with the SKIL TS6307, it includes more accessories, though the SKIL has a folding stand. For a hobbyist who wants to cut dadoes and crosscut without buying add-ons, it offers more at the same tier.

Ownership: check the blade alignment and fence parallel on arrival, since factory settings vary. Use the zero-clearance plate for thin stock and replace it when worn. Keep the rack clean, and always use the guard and riving knife.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want dado capability, a crosscut sled and a wheeled stand in one package.
pros: Dado plate, sled and zero-clearance plate included
Soft start reduces startup jolt on shared circuits
Wheeled stand makes moving the saw easy
Multi-material blade cuts wood and plastics
cons: No blade brake mentioned in the listing
Brand support is thinner than the big names

products.name: DEWALT DWE7485 15 Amp 8-1/4 Inch Compact Jobsite Table Saw
products.description:
A compact 8-1/4 inch saw trades blade size for weight and size, and the Site-Pro modular guarding system lets you adjust the guard and riving knife without tools, which encourages people to leave the guard on. A rack and pinion telescoping fence rail makes fence adjustments smooth and accurate, and 24.5 inches of rip capacity is enough to rip a 4x8 plywood sheet in half.

The smaller blade cuts about 2-1/2 inches deep, less than a 10 inch saw's 3-1/8 inches, which matters for 2x lumber thicker than 2 inches when a bevel is set. Compared with the Bosch GTS15-10, it rips narrower stock and has no brake, but it is lighter and easier to carry. For a finish carpenter who needs to move the saw through narrow doors and up stairs, the compact size is the selling point.

Ownership: use thin-kerf 8-1/4 inch blades, which are less common than 10 inch blades, so buy spares. Check the blade alignment and keep the table waxed. Clean sawdust from the guarding system, since tool-free joints jam when packed with dust.
products.bestFor: Finish carpenters who need a light, compact saw that fits through doors and up stairs.
pros: Compact body is easy to carry and store
Site-Pro guarding adjusts without tools
Rack and pinion fence adjusts quickly
24.5 inch rip handles half sheets of plywood
cons: 8-1/4 inch blade cuts shallower than 10 inch saws
No blade brake in the listing
Blades are less common than 10 inch sizes

products.name: SKIL TS6307-00 15 Amp 10 Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Folding Stand
products.description:
An integrated folding stand lets you set up the saw in seconds and fold it into a compact shape for transport, and rack and pinion fence rails keep the fence parallel to the blade. A micro-adjust feature lets you align the blade parallel to the fence and miter slot, which is the single most important setup for clean, safe rips. A 15 amp motor drives the 10 inch blade.

The tradeoff is feel and capacity. Compared with the Bosch GTS15-10, the SKIL has less rip capacity and a less refined fence, but it costs less. Against the Evolution R10TBLX, it lacks the dado plate and sled but has a folding stand rather than a wheeled one. If you move the saw often between jobs and set it up on uneven ground, the folding stand is convenient.

Ownership: check the blade parallel to the miter slot first, using the micro-adjust. Wax the table and keep the rails clean. Fold the stand carefully to avoid pinching, and store the saw dry. Use the riving knife for every cut, and never remove the guard.
products.bestFor: Contractors who move the saw often and want a folding stand with a micro-adjustable blade.
pros: Integrated folding stand sets up fast
Micro-adjust makes blade alignment easy
Rack and pinion rails keep the fence parallel
10 inch blade cuts full 2x lumber depth
cons: Less rip capacity than the Bosch
Fence feel is less refined than higher tiers
No dado plate or crosscut sled included

products.name: MarvTool 15 Amp 10 Inch Portable Table Saw, 4,600 RPM, 28.3 Pounds

specList.label: Cuts
specList.value: 90 degree crosscut and 0 to 45 degree bevel

products.description:
At 28.3 pounds, this is the lightest saw in the roundup, which makes it a bench-top or truck-bed tool rather than a full jobsite saw. The 15 amp motor spins a 36-tooth blade at about 4,600 RPM, fast for a table saw. Blade height and angle are adjustable, with a 90 degree crosscut and bevels from 0 to 45 degrees.

The tradeoff is stability and accuracy. A light saw on a bench vibrates more and walks, so clamp it down. A 36-tooth blade tears plywood, so replace it with a 50-tooth blade. Compared with the Bosch GTS15-10, it has much less rip capacity and no stand, but it costs a fraction. For a homeowner who needs a table saw for occasional trim and small boards, it is a sensible entry.

Ownership: set it up on a stable bench and clamp it, and check the blade parallel to the miter slot. Use push sticks for narrow rips, and keep the guard on. Check the fence for square before cutting, and expect to tune it more than the premium saws.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who need an occasional table saw and want the lightest, lowest-tier option.
pros: 28.3 pounds is the lightest saw in the roundup
15 amp motor at about 4,600 RPM cuts quickly
Blade height and bevel are adjustable
Lowest relative price in the roundup
cons: Light body vibrates and needs clamping to a bench
36-tooth blade tears plywood and needs replacing
Rip capacity and fence are limited

buyingCriteria.explanation: Rip capacity is the distance from the blade to the far end of the fence, and it sets the widest board you can rip. The Bosch GTS15-10 offers 32-1/8 inches, and the DEWALT DWE7485 24.5 inches. A 24 inch capacity splits a 4x8 sheet in half, and a 32 inch capacity lets you rip wider panels. Many buyers overlook this until they cannot rip a shelf board. Check the rip number against the fence on the side you will use, because some saws quote only the right side of the blade.

The fence determines accuracy and speed. A rack and pinion fence moves both ends together and stays parallel. The Bosch, DEWALT, SKIL and Evolution all use rack and pinion rails. A fence that creeps out of parallel causes burn marks and kickback. Run a test rip on scrap and measure the board at both ends with calipers; a gap larger than the thickness of a business card means the fence needs adjusting.

A brake stops the blade quickly after power off, and the Bosch stops it in about three seconds. Tool-free guarding like the DEWALT's Site-Pro makes it easy to keep the guard on. No saw in this guide has a flesh-sensing system, so guarding and push sticks are your protection. Whatever the saw, a push stick and a riving knife do more for safety than any extra feature.

A 10 inch blade cuts about 3-1/8 inches deep, and an 8-1/4 inch blade cuts about 2-1/2. The DEWALT DWE7485 uses 8-1/4 inch blades, which are less common. Choose the larger blade if you cut thick lumber or bevels. If you buy 8-1/4 inch blades, order two spares because local stores seldom stock them.

A folding stand sets up fast, a wheeled stand rolls easily, and a bench saw needs a bench. The SKIL has a folding stand, the Bosch and Evolution have wheeled stands, and the MarvTool needs a bench. Heavy saws need wheels. Weigh the stand together with the saw when you plan to lift it into a truck bed alone.

A dado plate lets you cut grooves, and a crosscut sled makes accurate crosscuts. The Evolution R10TBLX includes both. Buying them separately can cost as much as the saw's price difference. A dado stack also needs a wider insert and a lower depth setting, so check that the saw's arbor length allows it.

specDecoder.meaning: Rip capacity is the maximum distance from the blade to the fence. It limits board width.
specDecoder.watchFor: Listings quote it to the right of the blade only, so check which side. Check the claim against the fence stops at full extension.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps indicate motor draw. All five saws are 15 amps, the household circuit limit.
specDecoder.watchFor: Horsepower claims such as the Bosch's are peak figures, not continuous. A saw can be 15 amps and still be underpowered for wet pressure-treated lumber.

specDecoder.meaning: RPM is blade speed. Higher speed gives a smoother cut but needs a sharp blade.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MarvTool's 4,600 RPM is a no-load figure. Speed alone does not make a cut clean; blade tooth count does.

specDecoder.meaning: A gear drives both ends of the fence. It keeps the fence parallel to the blade.
specDecoder.watchFor: Cheap versions still need alignment checks. Test the rack on your saw by sliding the fence from one end to the other.

specDecoder.meaning: Soft start ramps the motor speed on startup. It reduces the jolt and circuit trips.
specDecoder.watchFor: It does not change cutting power. Soft start is useful on generators as well as house circuits.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rip capacity and fence
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rip capacity, from the DEWALT's 24.5 inches to the Bosch's 32-1/8 inches, and rated fence designs. A good fence matters more than motor size. We also noted whether the quoted capacity measured to the right of the blade or the left.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at brakes, guarding and riving knives. The Bosch has a brake, and the DEWALT has tool-free guarding. Tool-free guarding scored higher because guards left on prevent injuries.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability and stand
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stands and weights, from the 28.3 pound MarvTool to wheeled stands. A saw you cannot lift is not portable, so weight counted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Included accessories
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted included dado plates and sleds. The Evolution leads. Accessories that you would otherwise buy separately counted toward value.

howWeEvaluated.title: Relative value
howWeEvaluated.description: We used price tier to compare what extra spending buys. We never used listed prices in our comparison, only relative tiers.

cards.label: 10 inch blade
cards.text: Cuts about 3-1/8 inches deep and uses common blades. The Bosch, SKIL, Evolution and MarvTool use it.

cards.label: 8-1/4 inch blade
cards.text: Lighter and more compact, but cuts about 2-1/2 inches deep. The DEWALT DWE7485 uses it.

howToChoose.note: Choose 10 inch for thick lumber and 8-1/4 inch for light, portable work.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Plywood needs rip capacity of at least 24 inches, a stable table and outfeed support. Use a sharp 40-tooth or higher blade.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Bosch GTS15-10 rips the widest, and the DEWALT DWE7485 splits a sheet in half. The MarvTool is too small for sheets.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You rip daily or need a larger table. A contractor saw is the next step beyond the Bosch GTS15-10.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut a few boards a year. The MarvTool or SKIL covers that.

maintenance.interval: At setup and every few months
maintenance.why: A misaligned blade burns wood and causes kickback. Adjust until parallel. Use a square and a dial indicator if you have one.
A waxed table lets wood glide. Rust and pitch make it stick. Use paste wax, not silicone spray.
Dust jams the fence. A clean rack moves smoothly. A toothbrush works well.
A dull blade strains the motor and raises kickback risk. Sharp blades cut cleanly. Keep a spare blade ready.
A bent knife loses its protection. Replace it if bent. Never cut without it.

faq.q: Is a jobsite saw accurate enough for furniture?
faq.a: With careful setup, yes. A good fence and aligned blade are what matter. A cabinet saw is more stable for long rips. Adding an outfeed table helps long boards.
It buys a 10 inch saw with a rack and pinion fence and a stand. Listing prices move, so check the live cost. Expect to buy a better blade and push sticks as first accessories.

faq.q: How long do these saws last?
faq.a: With care, many years. Bearings and motors wear first. Store them dry and wax the table to prevent rust.
No. Flesh sensing exists only on SawStop saws. Use guards and push sticks. The Bosch brake stops the blade quickly but does not sense skin.

faq.q: Can I use a dado stack?
faq.a: Only with the correct dado plate. The Evolution includes one. Never run a dado stack without the correct plate.

faq.q: Why does my saw burn the wood?
faq.a: A dull blade or a misaligned fence causes burning. Check alignment first. Hardwood needs a sharper blade and slower feed.
